equation gibbs thomsonS_r = S_B exp[2σV_m/(rRT)]. S_r is crystallite solubility at radius r; S_B is bulk solubility, V_m molar volume, σ specific surface energy, R gas constant and T temperature.author derivedSource-reported observationmodelschwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 13212, Equation 3
basic acetate cluster hypothesisEarly noncrystalline absorption is attributed to basic zinc-acetate clusters. Zn4O(OAc)6 and Zn10O4(OAc)12 are cited ethanol structures; analogous DMSO precursors are proposed, not directly identified in this study.author derivedSource-reported observationmodelschwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 7, printed p. 13211, IV.A
dopant exclusion inferenceCritical surviving nuclei exclude dopants; subsequent surface binding and OH− reaction incorporate Co nearly isotropically during growth. This is inferred from spectral titration, not an atom-by-atom dopant map.author derivedSource-reported observationmodelschwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 13212, IV.B; schwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 9, printed p. 13213, IV.B continuation
scheme1 scopeScheme 1 contrasts surviving undoped ZnO nuclei followed by surface Co binding/growth with inhibited direct nucleation from Co-containing precursors. The circles and symbols are mechanistic illustrations, not measured structure coordinates.author derivedSource-reported observationmodelschwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 13212, Scheme 1
coordination barrier rationalePseudo-octahedral dopants in basic acetate precursors must convert to tetrahedral ZnO coordination, adding a nucleation barrier. The authors also emphasize reduced thermodynamic driving force from impurity strain.author derivedSource-reported observationmodelschwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 13212, IV.B
strain solubility rationaleSurface/near-surface dopants increase strain and specific surface energy, increasing solubility and the critical nucleation radius and lowering metastable final dimensions. No numerical σ, solubility, critical radius or activation energy is fitted.author derivedSource-reported observationmodelschwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 13212, Equation 3 discussion; schwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 9, printed p. 13213, Continuation
surface intermediate assignmentA broad intermediate is assigned to inhomogeneous tetrahedral Co bound at ZnO surfaces, as monomers or basic-acetate fragments, before incorporation by hydroxide. Comparison to excess-acetate Co in DMSO supports stronger acetate than lattice-oxide ligand fields.author derivedSource-reported observationmodelschwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 13212, IV.B
base consumption inferenceBand-gap intensity versus added base extrapolates nearly through the origin after nucleation, suggesting most added hydroxide forms ZnO rather than persistent molecular precursors. Internal-Co intensity instead intercepts near 0.36 equivalent, supporting initial core exclusion.author derivedSource-reported observationmodelschwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 7, printed p. 13211, Figure 11 and discussion; schwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 13212, Continuation
spatial homogeneity limitNearly isotropic incorporation during growth and homogeneous substitutional spectroscopy do not imply uniform dopant content in the initial undoped critical nucleus or zero lattice defects.author derivedSource-reported observationmodelschwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 1, printed p. 13205, Abstract; schwartz2003 · Main PDF p. 8, printed p. 13212, IV.B
